nodes.title: Uniform integral tricanonical equations
nodes.statement: Let S be a quasi-compact Noetherian scheme, g≥2, and f:X→S a stable genus-g family. Put E=f_*ω³, of rank r=5g−5, and use the quotient convention for i:X↪P_S(E), with i*O(1)=ω³. For the ideal sheaf I of i there is d₀≥2 such that for every integer d≥d₀, I(d) is relatively generated, R^jπ_*I(d)=0 for j>0, and K_d=π_*I(d) is finite locally free and commutes with every base change. There is a base-change-compatible exact sequence 0→K_d→Sym^d E→f_*ω^{3d}→0, whose quotient has rank (6d−1)(g−1). Evaluation of K_d generates I(d), and its geometric-fibre equations recover the embedded curve as a closed subscheme. The same d₀ works over every residue characteristic of S, without assuming S is reduced, integral or flat over Z.
hypotheses: Stable means proper flat finitely presented, geometrically connected nodal fibres and relatively ample dualizing line; genus g≥2 is fixed.
The MC.1 tricanonical embedding and its locally free direct images commute with arbitrary base change.
π:P_S(E)→S uses one-dimensional quotients, so π_*O(d)=Sym^d E for d≥0.
proofSteps: In 0→I→O_P→i_*O_X→0, the last two terms are S-flat, hence so is I. Tensoring with any base change stays exact, identifying I_T with the actual ideal of X_T. This is the flat-kernel criterion, not an appeal to constancy of a Hilbert polynomial.

Choose a finite affine cover trivializing E. Apply the imported relative Serre and S-flat family-regularity theorems on each projective-space chart to I. Take the maximum of these finitely many regularity thresholds: each conclusion holds for every higher degree on the same fixed chart. Descent gives one d₀ on S.

Push forward the twisted ideal sequence. The higher vanishing supplies surjectivity; projective-bundle cohomology identifies the middle term with Sym^d E. Cohomology and arbitrary base change for the stable family identify the quotient with f_*ω^{3d}.

Local freeness of the quotient makes the exact sequence locally split as modules; arbitrary pullback therefore preserves its kernel. Relative generation, also pulled back, recovers the fibre ideal sheaf. Equality of degree-d subspaces gives equality of these ideal sheaves after untwisting.

This refines the proof obligation of the parent finite-degree-equations node. It does not create another generic relative Serre theorem or assert generation of all lower graded pieces of the homogeneous ideal.
acceptance: Choose d once before applying any characteristic-dependent positivity argument.
The degree-d equations determine the saturated closed-subscheme ideal, not necessarily the entire graded ideal in lower degrees.

nodes.title: One determinant line over the integer base
nodes.statement: Let M be the proper coarse algebraic space of the stable genus-g stack over Z, g≥2. Let V→M̄_g be a representable finite surjective scheme cover, and put h:V→M. Fix any d at least the bound of integral-hilbert-kernel for the pulled-back family, and λ=det f_*ω^{3d} on V. Suppose the generic positivity supplier gives the parent moduli-determinant-ample criterion in every characteristic, and there are a line L on M and e>0 with h*L≅λ^e. Then λ is ample over Z, L is ample over Z, and M is a projective Z-scheme. Neither V nor its fibres need be integral for this argument.
hypotheses: M̄_g is proper finite type Deligne–Mumford over Z, with finite inertia.
The finite scheme-cover and coarse power-descent contracts are separate inputs, not consequences of coarse-space existence.
The determinant and its descent power are fixed before testing fibres.
proofSteps: Properness of the stack and finiteness of V→M̄_g imply V is a proper finite-type Z-scheme. The composite h is proper and quasi-finite, hence finite; its geometric fibres have finitely many points by the finite stack cover and the coarse geometric-point property.

Apply the fixed-degree multiplication and ideal comparison on every V_s over an algebraically closed residue field. The family has finite coarse moduli fibres, so the parent ampleness criterion makes λ_s ample. Reduce nilpotents and components only through the generic criterion, without assuming the total cover normal.

Apply fixed-line openness of ampleness to λ on the proper scheme V over Spec Z (Stacks 0D2N). The resulting open sets cover Spec Z; relative ampleness is local on the base, so this single λ is relatively ample. No comparison between λ_{3d} for different d is used.

The same holds for λ^e=h*L. Descend relative ampleness across the finite surjection h using the generic algebraic-space finite descent theorem. An algebraic space carrying such a relatively ample line over Spec Z is a scheme and is projective.

Only after projectivity and irreducibility choose a dominating component and normalize to obtain the parent normal integral projective cover. This removes the potential circular use of irreducibility to construct the initial parameter scheme.
acceptance: Do not replace the initial cover by an integral dominating component before irreducibility has been proved.
No arbitrary-base-change theorem for coarse spaces is used; the family direct images do commute with arbitrary base change.

nodes.title: Jacobi level as an abelian Teichmuller component
nodes.statement: Fix g≥2 and N≥3, B=Spec Z[1/N], and G=(Z/N)^{2g}. On the smooth genus-g stack the sheaf of exterior epimorphisms from the prime-to-residue-characteristic fundamental group to G is the full abelian torsion-frame sheaf, after the canonical H¹/Jacobian dual-and-Tate-twist comparisons. In this sheaf the homogeneous symplectic-similitude frames form an open and closed subfunctor, stable under GSp_{2g}(Z/N). Its multiplier map has target the primitive-pairing scheme B_N=Spec Z[1/N,ζ_N]. Fixing a B_N-point gives exactly the symplectic Jacobi-level problem; the unconditioned sheaf of all frames is larger. Pairing conventions use e_N:J[N]×J[N]→μ_N, whereas DM 5.3 uses the H¹ pairing with values in μ_N^{-1}.
hypotheses: Import the relative Jacobian, canonical polarization and arbitrary pullback on the Noetherian MC.1 atlas from JC1, and effective polarized-family descent from R09.4.
N is invertible, so torsion and frame sheaves are finite étale; the comparison is étale-local and natural in the base.
The primitive root is part of the base change, not a choice silently made over B.
proofSteps: Use relative Kummer theory to identify J[N] with R¹f_*μ_N, and duality between H¹ with constant coefficients and the abelianized fundamental group modulo N. Exterior conjugation is trivial because G is abelian.
An epimorphism to G from the rank-2g abelianization modulo N is an isomorphism: a surjection of finite free modules of equal finite cardinality has zero kernel, including composite N.
Transport the cup-product orientation through the dual and Tate twist. Retain its inverse on changing between the H¹ and torsion conventions; test rather than erase this sign/twist.

Étale-locally all relevant sheaves are finite constant, so the condition that an isomorphism takes the symplectic form to a scalar multiple is a union of connected components. The scalar is primitive and defines the multiplier morphism.
Fixing the multiplier gives the symplectic level problem; the full GL-frame sheaf is a finite union of translates of the homogeneous subfunctor. This comparison is used only over the smooth locus.
acceptance: Do not call all GL frames symplectic similitudes when g≥2.
An H¹-level frame and a torsion frame require the specified dual and twist; a literal identification of their pairings is wrong.

sources.match: Jacobi level is an open-and-closed part of abelian Teichmuller level, and the multiplier separates the fixed symplectic problems.

nodes.title: Tame normalization of a fixed pairing level
nodes.statement: Over B_N=Spec Z[1/N,ζ_N], let U be the smooth genus-g stack and U_N its fixed-pairing Jacobi-level cover, g≥2 and N≥3. Normalize the stable stack M̄_g×B_N in U_N, retaining every generic component. The resulting stack Y is finite over M̄_g×B_N, proper and flat of finite presentation over B_N; every geometric fibre of Y is normal, and U_N is dense in every such fibre. Consequently its geometric fibre component count is locally constant on B_N and equals that of U_N. Y is not asserted to be a scheme, a smooth stack, or a naive nodal full-level moduli problem.
hypotheses: The parent MC.1 boundary charts are excellent regular schemes, smooth over the integer base, with a relative normal-crossing boundary. Its generic divisorial points have characteristic zero, as required by the absolute local Lemma 5.10 of DM.
The DM tame Teichmuller normalization theorem applies to G=(Z/N)^{2g}, whose order N^{2g} is invertible on B_N.
Use the exact finite normalization and normal-component comparison supplier contracts; no arbitrary normalization/base-change claim is made.
proofSteps: Use the open-and-closed abelian Teichmuller comparison to select the fixed-pairing component before normalization. Normalize each generic component and descend the finite normalization from étale atlases (R09.5).

Apply the tame local theorem of DM 5.9–5.10. On strict local normal-crossing charts, the cover is dominated by adjoining roots of the boundary parameters of order invertible on the residue base, and the normalization is obtained by the appropriate finite tame quotient.

The generic Kummer-chart supplier must give flatness and geometrically normal fibres after taking this quotient; its proof uses the root charts, tame invariants and normality. This is the explicit SF.1 extension request, not a consequence of normalization being finite.

The nonempty smooth part is dense on every geometric fibre by those same boundary charts. Apply the proper-flat-geometrically-normal component-count theorem DM 4.17(iii), pp.102–103, and its application in 5.11, p.107. Use 4.16 for irreducibility of normal connected components; 4.19 is instead the valuative criterion for properness.
A normal Noetherian geometric fibre has disjoint irreducible components, so deleting this dense boundary complement preserves its connected-component count.
acceptance: The tame hypothesis concerns G of order N^{2g}, not the order of GL or Sp acting on its frames.
In characteristic 2, level 3 is admissible even though Sp₄(F₃) has even order.
Geometrically normal fibres are a theorem of the Kummer local description; ordinary normalization alone does not imply it.

sources.locator: Theorem 5.9 and local Lemma 5.10, pp.106–107; Corollary 5.11, p.107; 5.15, pp.108–109; Proposition 4.16 and Theorem 4.17, pp.102–103; normalization after 4.20, pp.103–104
sources.match: The tame normalization and proper component-count route transfers connectedness to every admissible characteristic. The statement is an application of this route, not fine representability on the boundary.

nodes.title: The complex fixed-pairing orbit calculation
nodes.statement: Let g≥2, N≥3 and ζ_N∈C be primitive. Assuming the generic marked-surface uniformization and integral symplectic-reduction supplier contracts, the analytification of the fixed-pairing smooth curve level scheme is connected: its components correspond to orbits of the orientation-preserving genus-g mapping class group on symplectic frames modulo N, and that action is transitive. This complex calculation together with boundary-level-normalization proves every geometric fibre over B_N is connected.
hypotheses: Use the actual analytification of the MC.4 fine smooth scheme, with the H¹/torsion convention of jacobi-teichmueller-comparison.
The Teichmuller space is connected; its mapping-class quotient supplies the analytic moduli comparison, rather than an assumed connected moduli space.
The integral symplectic reduction Sp_{2g}(Z)→Sp_{2g}(Z/N) is onto for composite N as well as prime N.
proofSteps: Use connected marked Teichmuller space and identify the analytic moduli cover as the quotient of its product with the finite set of frames. Components are the mapping-class orbits of that finite set.

The mapping-class action on integral first homology surjects onto Sp_{2g}(Z) (DM 5.12). Reduce modulo N; use elementary symplectic generators over Z/N, or Chinese remainder and prime-power generators, rather than a finite-field-only argument.
The symplectic group acts transitively on its own frame torsor, so there is one orbit. Connected analytification implies connectedness of the algebraic complex fibre.

Since B_N is connected, the locally constant component count from boundary-level-normalization equals one everywhere. Geometric normality plus density then gives connectedness of the smooth fibre, and smoothness makes it irreducible.
acceptance: Fix the primitive pairing before computing orbits; homogeneous level can have several multiplier components.
The cited upstream Fuchsian and topology layers do not themselves contain Teichmuller theory or this homology-action theorem. Their precise Part II extensions remain explicit requests and gaps.

sources.match: DM reduces component counts to the connected marked space and the symplectic orbit calculation. The Weil and Manger inputs it cites have not been read at their original sources here.

gaps.title: Generic vector positivity and the Grassmann ampleness lemma
gaps.detail: CLM generic background has been read. Existing AlgebraicVectorBundles L0 gives symmetric powers/determinants and SF.5 gives line nefness, not this vector criterion or det-Q ampleness theorem. The contracts and their proof ingredients are assigned as proposed SF foundations extensions; no implementation or accepted new owner node exists yet.

gaps.title: Surface theorems and the unstable pointed transport step
gaps.detail: Ekedahl and Chen–Zhang primary versions are now acquired and read at the indicated statements. Their generic dependencies and the char-zero vanishing source still require supplier decomposition. In the pointed proof, contraction can make previously disjoint markings meet; the coefficient of an exceptional divisor is m minus the sum of coefficients meeting its centre, which need not be nonnegative merely from each a_i≤m. The parent is not closed until a model argument handles those collisions and the ensuing direct-image exactness. Do not extend special-fibre H¹-vanishing to arbitrary unstable nodal curves.

gaps.title: Tame Kummer normal-fibre supplier
gaps.detail: The DM proof has been read, including the finite abelian group route avoiding a prime-to-order condition on the symplectic deck group. Its local normality, flatness and component-count theorem remain generic contracts; finite normalization in R09.5 supplies none of these by itself.

sourceIssues.printed: The pointed induction claims R¹f_*ω^m(D_j)=0 from fibre degrees on a general nodal family with smooth generic fibre.
sourceIssues.correction: Retain the nefness target, but replace this vanishing step by a proved pointed model/transport or logarithmic positivity argument. The generic evaluation-image repair of Corollary 6.6 does not by itself give the required exact sequence.
sourceIssues.reason: Blow up a constant smooth genus-g≥2 family at a point of a special fibre. At D_j=0 the exceptional rational tail has degree −m for ω^m and H¹ of dimension m−1. The normalization sequence surjects special-fibre H¹ onto this group, whereas generic H¹ is zero. Top-degree cohomology/base change then precludes the asserted global R¹ vanishing. This is the additional Proposition 6.7 use of the phenomenon in parent E12.

review.reason: Confirmed in the 1 July 2021 manuscript, Proposition 6.7 p.26. For the blowup of C×P¹ at a special-fibre point, with C smooth of genus at least two and no markings yet, the exceptional P¹ has relative dualizing degree −1. Its m-th power contributes H¹ of dimension m−1, and the normalization sequence maps fibre H¹ onto it. The generic H¹ is zero; top-degree base change forces nonzero R¹. This refutes the displayed vanishing step, not the nefness conclusion. No claim of historical novelty or publisher-version agreement is made.
